recent_commits.message: Fixes for #506 and #523: output search limit, sandbox folders, writes beside the script, SPSS encoding (0.4.1.3)
recent_commits.body:
- reproducibility_check searches only the first 20,000 lines of a script's
  printed output for statistical results (option
  metacheck.repro_output_max_lines) and says so in the report (#523, item 2).
  On the SURF server sq8y6's script was stopped after 300 s as it should be,
  but the search through its printed output then kept the job busy until the
  60-minute job limit.
- Docker sandbox: R's cache, configuration and data folders are put in /tmp
  (the home folder is read-only, so renv::restore() stopped), and
  RSTUDIO_PANDOC points to the Pandoc Quarto has in the image (#523, items 4
  and 5).
- Package layout: a quoted relative path whose folder exists from the
  script's own or .Rproj folder, but not from the top, is rewritten to its
  path from the top, so writes beside the script work and later scripts find
  the file (#523, item 3).
- codebook_check: mapply(USE.NAMES = FALSE), so an NA variable name no longer
  stops it with "row names contain missing values" (#523, item 1).
- .sav files with Windows (CP1252) text are read again as CP1252 (#523,
  item 6).
- dryad_info(cache = TRUE) does not reuse listings stored before the paging
  fix of 0.3.3.1, or marked incomplete (#506).

recent_commits.message: report(): find Quarto's Pandoc on Linux (bin/tools/<arch>/)
recent_commits.body:
.report_pandoc_dir() looked only in <quarto>/bin/tools/, where Quarto keeps
Pandoc on Windows and macOS. On Linux it is in bin/tools/x86_64/ or
bin/tools/aarch64/, so the checklist, simple and brief reports failed on a
Linux server without a separate Pandoc. Checked on the TU/e Shiny server
(Quarto 1.6.40): before NULL, now bin/tools/x86_64.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Add functions for PsyArXiv's own API (psyarxiv_*)
recent_commits.body:
PsyArXiv now has its own read-only API (https://next.psyarxiv.org/api,
no key). New functions next to the OSF route, which is unchanged:
psyarxiv_search() (full-text search, filters, paging), psyarxiv_info()
(full records: data/prereg/materials statements, COI, supplements
project, file links), psyarxiv_versions(), psyarxiv_author(),
psyarxiv_download(), psyarxiv_dumps()/psyarxiv_dump() (yearly bulk
files), psyarxiv_subjects(), psyarxiv_licenses(). Ids are OSF guids;
links and PsyArXiv DOIs are accepted. The address is the option
metacheck.psyarxiv.api. Tests use recorded answers in
apis/next.psyarxiv.org; downloads are tested live (skipped on CRAN).

recent_commits.message: Replace sd_type with sd_meaning and add an SE premise
recent_commits.body:
* sd_type = c("sample", "population", "either") becomes sd_meaning = c("sd_sample", "sd_pop", "sd_sample_or_pop", "se") in grimmer(), debit(), and all their mappers, explanations, and plots. Each value is one premise about what a value reported as an SD really is: an SD of some kind, or a misreported SE.
* "se" is the standard error of the mean, the sample SD divided by sqrt(n). Its rounding bounds are transformed, not the reported value: sd_denominator() gives n * (n - 1) for it, and every path from the reported value to a sum of squares or a binary spread goes through that function.
* One argument rather than a second, combinable one, because few combinations of statistic and denominator occur in practice; a new premise of the same form is one row in sd_denominator().
* Brute-force tests check GRIMMER and DEBIT under "se" against every reachable sample.
* The docs warn that the test is weak under "se": from about n = 20 on, nearly every GRIM-consistent value set passes.

* An error there now names row 1 if row 2 passes the test. An error about the arguments, such as a missing `digits_x`, fails on every row and still names none.

recent_commits.message: Keep only character row names of a data frame passed to a mapper
recent_commits.body:
* Integer row names, as left by `data[rows, ]`, counted as non-automatic, so a common base R subset gained a `rowname` column of row numbers.
* A data frame with row names and a `rowname` column failed with dplyr's "duplicate names" error; it now says what clashes.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add dots to the example audit() methods
recent_commits.body: * The example `audit()` methods in `?audit_cols_minimal` and the simple extension vignette take the dots, as the generic now requires; a package copying `function(data)` got an S3 consistency warning from R CMD check.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Read the dispersed variables from the settings in audit_seq()
recent_commits.body:
* e9af559 moved `var` from the "scrutiny" attribute into its settings tibble, but the branch for output with rows still read `meta$var`. It fell back to the `var` column, so a variable whose dispersion `out_min` or `out_max` clipped away in every case lost its `hits_*` and `diff_*` columns.
* Both branches now read it from the settings, once.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add audit(.by) and explain a class lost to group_by()
recent_commits.body:
* audit() is now audit(data, ..., .by = NULL). With .by, it splits data with [, which keeps class and attribute, summarizes each group, and binds the results behind the grouping columns, in order of appearance.
* group_by() drops the mapper class but keeps the attribute, so audit.default() and explain_map.default() recognize such data and point to the output from before grouping. Other data get a plain no-method error instead of R's.
* Every audit() method takes the dots now, as R CMD check requires; the extension vignette shows the new signature.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return the recorded settings as a tibble from scrutiny_meta()
recent_commits.body:
* The "scrutiny" attribute records a settings tibble: setting, value, default, and added_by. Sequence and total-n mappers append their own settings, such as dispersion, which were not recorded before.
* scrutiny_meta() shows each value as R code in single quotes, which pillar prints without escaping. Package code reads typed values with the internal scrutiny_args().
* default compares each value to the defaults evaluated when the factory made the mapper, so the print header no longer needs the mapper passed in. The bookkeeping for audit_seq() stays in the attribute but out of the tibble; var is now a settings row.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Print the settings header with a single space after the name
recent_commits.body: * pillar pads header names to the widest, "A tibble", unless none is named, so the methods write the names into the lines themselves.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Name non-default settings in the print header of mapper output
recent_commits.body:
* pillar::tbl_sum() methods for the four basic mapper classes compare the recorded args with the mapper's own defaults, so the attribute needs no new element. Sequence and total-n output gets the line through the basic class.
* scrutiny_meta()'s docs say which elements every mapper records and which only sequence mappers add, and that items_averaged and the digits are columns, not args.
* Unlink the write_doc_audit*() topics, which are no longer documented.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Update two tests for debit_map(show_rec)
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Explain multi-item percentages under items_averaged
recent_commits.body: * Percent correct on a k-item test and pooled proportions over k trials need items_averaged = k, so 1 is not right for every percentage.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add an article on interpreting results
recent_commits.body:
* Lists the benign causes of an inconsistency (rounding, sample size, scale items, SD convention, other totals, non-integer data, typos), with the scrutiny call that checks each.
* Lays out the workflow from mapper to audit, seq, explanations, and scrutiny_meta(), and says how to weigh and report the evidence.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Mark new functions experimental, state a stability policy, and unexport write_doc_audit*()
recent_commits.body:
* Every export new since 0.6.1 carries the experimental badge; functions released before keep their status.
* The pkgdown reference index says developer tools may change in minor releases.
* write_doc_audit(), write_doc_audit_seq(), and write_doc_audit_total_n() generate roxygen text and serve no analysis, so they are internal now. The extension vignette points to the help pages for the conventions instead.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Name the row of data in per-row mapper errors
recent_commits.body:
* function_map() re-signals the test's error in place of purrr's indexed one, adding the row. Total-n mappers translate the scenario row into the row of data.
* Document that percent applies per call, with a split-and-bind example, and that total-n digits apply to every row.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Hide debit_map()'s reconstructed values by default
recent_commits.body:
* show_rec now defaults to FALSE, as in grim_map(), so the eight bound and sum columns are only returned on request.
* debit_plot() recomputes them under the recorded settings when they are missing, so plotting default output still works.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Make seq_disperse() return numbers and drop string_output
recent_commits.body:
* The strings were a holdover from when the mappers took x as a string. The mappers already passed string_output = "auto" with a numeric x, so their output is unchanged.
* A string from still sets the step size, trailing zeros included; the docs point to by for a number like 5.30.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Drop the global variables of function_duplicate_cols()
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Remove duplicate_detect()
recent_commits.body:
* Superseded since 0.3.0 by duplicate_tally(), which counts duplicates instead of only flagging them.
* With one product left, function_duplicate_cols() is inlined into duplicate_tally(), whose file is renamed to match it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Remove the deprecated tolerance argument
recent_commits.body: * grim(), grimmer(), and their mappers compare exact integers, so the argument never had an effect. Removing it at 1.0.0 saves carrying the deprecation to 2.0.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Export scrutiny_meta()
recent_commits.body:
* The "scrutiny" attribute records the settings of the call that produced
a mapper's output, but nothing exported read it, so a report could not
state the rounding method or SD convention behind a verdict. The internal
accessor moves to its own file with documentation of the list's elements.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Record reported verdicts for audit_seq() instead of re-testing
recent_commits.body:
* The sequence mapper stores the verdict of every input row from its
initial test as `results_reported` in the "scrutiny" attribute, and
`audit_seq()` indexes it by `case`.

* `audit_seq()` used to recover the mapper's name from a class string,
look the function up in the caller's environment, and replay the
call's arguments from a `fun_args` element, so a dropped argument could
flip the verdict and the mapper had to be findable from wherever
`audit_seq()` ran. `find_fun_by_name()` and `fun_args` are gone; output
that has lost the attribute errors, as `explain_map()` does.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Accept any data frame as mapper input
recent_commits.body:
* `check_tibble()` rejected a `data.frame` with a conversion hint, so
tables from `read.csv()` or a PDF extractor failed on the first call.
It is now `as_tibble_input()`, which coerces any data frame to a
tibble and keeps non-automatic row names as a `rowname` column, since
a tibble has none and study labels would otherwise be lost in silence.
Anything that is not a data frame is still an error.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Make audit() reach every tier and guard study-level GRIM statistics
recent_commits.body:
* Sequence and total-n output carries the basic mapper's class after
its tier classes, so `audit()` dispatched to the basic method, which
counted the dispersed rows as reported cases and only printed a hint.
`audit.scrutiny_map_seq()` and `audit.scrutiny_map_total_n()` now call
`audit_seq()` and `audit_total_n()`.

* `grim_binomial()` and `grim_plot_rates()` reject sequence and total-n
output through `check_grim_map_basic()`: their rows are hypothetical
value sets, inconsistent by construction, so a p-value or rate over
them said nothing about the study, and was returned without a word.

* `check_audit_special()` is removed and `audit_cols_minimal()` loses
`name_test`; both only served the hint that `audit()` no longer needs.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix the review items of Oct 25
recent_commits.body:
* function_map() marked its error about a .fun whose arguments shadow
its internals as internal, which asked the user to report a bug. A user's
.fun with an argument named `data` triggers it, so it now goes through
abort_in_export() like the other checks at creation.

* map_value_sets() returns an empty vector for a wrapper with no formals
instead of failing on an empty cache key.

* .gitignore: `special-scripts/` made the three entries after it
redundant.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename vectorize_test() to map_value_sets()
recent_commits.body:
* It returns values, not a function, so it is no kind of Vectorize(); and
it serves grim_values(), grim_closest(), add_up_to(), and
is_percentage_of() too, which are no consistency tests.
* Drop the `frame` argument: it is always the caller's frame.
* Cache the missing() calls by the formals' names rather than the name the
wrapper was called under, which needed an identity check and an
empty-name branch. This makes fn_name_from_call() unused, so remove it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Run `jarl check . --fix --allow-dirty` and partly follow it
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Ignore special-scripts/
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Run tests in parallel
recent_commits.body:
* Config/testthat/parallel: true runs the test files in separate
processes. The number of them is TESTTHAT_CPUS, 2 by default.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

**Text, section, table and statistic extraction from academic papers (PDF, DOCX, HTML), built
for meta-science.**

interleaved columns, Greek letters decoded as Latin), identifies the paper's sections, pulls
tables out as cell grids, flattens table rows into records a statistics checker can read, and
renders the whole paper as Markdown. Every output carries a record of what the library had to
guess or refused

OIF (Output It Forward) is a Chrome extension that helps researchers detect and document open data indicators in scholarly articles while they browse. As you read a paper, OIF automatically scans the page for phrases and repository links commonly associated with open data practices, and logs matches to a running CSV file for systematic documentation.

highlights.message: Update README
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Replace sd_type with sd_meaning and add an SE premise
highlights.body:
* sd_type = c("sample", "population", "either") becomes sd_meaning = c("sd_sample", "sd_pop", "sd_sample_or_pop", "se") in grimmer(), debit(), and all their mappers, explanations, and plots. Each value is one premise about what a value reported as an SD really is: an SD of some kind, or a misreported SE.
* "se" is the standard error of the mean, the sample SD divided by sqrt(n). Its rounding bounds are transformed, not the reported value: sd_denominator() gives n * (n - 1) for it, and every path from the reported value to a sum of squares or a binary spread goes through that function.
* One argument rather than a second, combinable one, because few combinations of statistic and denominator occur in practice; a new premise of the same form is one row in sd_denominator().
* Brute-force tests check GRIMMER and DEBIT under "se" against every reachable sample.
* The docs warn that the test is weak under "se": from about n = 20 on, nearly every GRIM-consistent value set passes.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Tell basic settings from tier settings by name in scrutiny_args()
highlights.body:
* scrutiny_args() took the rows added by the same mapper as the first row. If a basic mapper recorded no settings, the first row was the sequence or total-n mapper's, whose settings were then read as the basic ones.
* The function_map() comment on missing values says where such a value can still come from: a .fun written elsewhere with a lifecycle::deprecated() default.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Name row 1 in a mapper error that is about that row
highlights.body:
* The first row is tested on its own before the others, outside the handler that names the row, so only errors in later rows said where they came from.
* An error there now names row 1 if row 2 passes the test. An error about the arguments, such as a missing `digits_x`, fails on every row and still names none.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Keep only character row names of a data frame passed to a mapper
highlights.body:
* Integer row names, as left by `data[rows, ]`, counted as non-automatic, so a common base R subset gained a `rowname` column of row numbers.
* A data frame with row names and a `rowname` column failed with dplyr's "duplicate names" error; it now says what clashes.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Add dots to the example audit() methods
highlights.body: * The example `audit()` methods in `?audit_cols_minimal` and the simple extension vignette take the dots, as the generic now requires; a package copying `function(data)` got an S3 consistency warning from R CMD check.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Read the dispersed variables from the settings in audit_seq()
highlights.body:
* e9af559 moved `var` from the "scrutiny" attribute into its settings tibble, but the branch for output with rows still read `meta$var`. It fell back to the `var` column, so a variable whose dispersion `out_min` or `out_max` clipped away in every case lost its `hits_*` and `diff_*` columns.
* Both branches now read it from the settings, once.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Add audit(.by) and explain a class lost to group_by()
highlights.body:
* audit() is now audit(data, ..., .by = NULL). With .by, it splits data with [, which keeps class and attribute, summarizes each group, and binds the results behind the grouping columns, in order of appearance.
* group_by() drops the mapper class but keeps the attribute, so audit.default() and explain_map.default() recognize such data and point to the output from before grouping. Other data get a plain no-method error instead of R's.
* Every audit() method takes the dots now, as R CMD check requires; the extension vignette shows the new signature.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Return the recorded settings as a tibble from scrutiny_meta()
highlights.body:
* The "scrutiny" attribute records a settings tibble: setting, value, default, and added_by. Sequence and total-n mappers append their own settings, such as dispersion, which were not recorded before.
* scrutiny_meta() shows each value as R code in single quotes, which pillar prints without escaping. Package code reads typed values with the internal scrutiny_args().
* default compares each value to the defaults evaluated when the factory made the mapper, so the print header no longer needs the mapper passed in. The bookkeeping for audit_seq() stays in the attribute but out of the tibble; var is now a settings row.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Print the settings header with a single space after the name
highlights.body: * pillar pads header names to the widest, "A tibble", unless none is named, so the methods write the names into the lines themselves.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Name non-default settings in the print header of mapper output
highlights.body:
* pillar::tbl_sum() methods for the four basic mapper classes compare the recorded args with the mapper's own defaults, so the attribute needs no new element. Sequence and total-n output gets the line through the basic class.
* scrutiny_meta()'s docs say which elements every mapper records and which only sequence mappers add, and that items_averaged and the digits are columns, not args.
* Unlink the write_doc_audit*() topics, which are no longer documented.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Update two tests for debit_map(show_rec)
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Explain multi-item percentages under items_averaged
highlights.body: * Percent correct on a k-item test and pooled proportions over k trials need items_averaged = k, so 1 is not right for every percentage.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Add an article on interpreting results
highlights.body:
* Lists the benign causes of an inconsistency (rounding, sample size, scale items, SD convention, other totals, non-integer data, typos), with the scrutiny call that checks each.
* Lays out the workflow from mapper to audit, seq, explanations, and scrutiny_meta(), and says how to weigh and report the evidence.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Mark new functions experimental, state a stability policy, and unexport write_doc_audit*()
highlights.body:
* Every export new since 0.6.1 carries the experimental badge; functions released before keep their status.
* The pkgdown reference index says developer tools may change in minor releases.
* write_doc_audit(), write_doc_audit_seq(), and write_doc_audit_total_n() generate roxygen text and serve no analysis, so they are internal now. The extension vignette points to the help pages for the conventions instead.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Name the row of data in per-row mapper errors
highlights.body:
* function_map() re-signals the test's error in place of purrr's indexed one, adding the row. Total-n mappers translate the scenario row into the row of data.
* Document that percent applies per call, with a split-and-bind example, and that total-n digits apply to every row.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Hide debit_map()'s reconstructed values by default
highlights.body:
* show_rec now defaults to FALSE, as in grim_map(), so the eight bound and sum columns are only returned on request.
* debit_plot() recomputes them under the recorded settings when they are missing, so plotting default output still works.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Make seq_disperse() return numbers and drop string_output
highlights.body:
* The strings were a holdover from when the mappers took x as a string. The mappers already passed string_output = "auto" with a numeric x, so their output is unchanged.
* A string from still sets the step size, trailing zeros included; the docs point to by for a number like 5.30.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Drop the global variables of function_duplicate_cols()
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Remove duplicate_detect()
highlights.body:
* Superseded since 0.3.0 by duplicate_tally(), which counts duplicates instead of only flagging them.
* With one product left, function_duplicate_cols() is inlined into duplicate_tally(), whose file is renamed to match it.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Remove the deprecated tolerance argument
highlights.body: * grim(), grimmer(), and their mappers compare exact integers, so the argument never had an effect. Removing it at 1.0.0 saves carrying the deprecation to 2.0.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Export scrutiny_meta()
highlights.body:
* The "scrutiny" attribute records the settings of the call that produced
a mapper's output, but nothing exported read it, so a report could not
state the rounding method or SD convention behind a verdict. The internal
accessor moves to its own file with documentation of the list's elements.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Record reported verdicts for audit_seq() instead of re-testing
highlights.body:
* The sequence mapper stores the verdict of every input row from its
initial test as `results_reported` in the "scrutiny" attribute, and
`audit_seq()` indexes it by `case`.

* `audit_seq()` used to recover the mapper's name from a class string,
look the function up in the caller's environment, and replay the
call's arguments from a `fun_args` element, so a dropped argument could
flip the verdict and the mapper had to be findable from wherever
`audit_seq()` ran. `find_fun_by_name()` and `fun_args` are gone; output
that has lost the attribute errors, as `explain_map()` does.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Accept any data frame as mapper input
highlights.body:
* `check_tibble()` rejected a `data.frame` with a conversion hint, so
tables from `read.csv()` or a PDF extractor failed on the first call.
It is now `as_tibble_input()`, which coerces any data frame to a
tibble and keeps non-automatic row names as a `rowname` column, since
a tibble has none and study labels would otherwise be lost in silence.
Anything that is not a data frame is still an error.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Make audit() reach every tier and guard study-level GRIM statistics
highlights.body:
* Sequence and total-n output carries the basic mapper's class after
its tier classes, so `audit()` dispatched to the basic method, which
counted the dispersed rows as reported cases and only printed a hint.
`audit.scrutiny_map_seq()` and `audit.scrutiny_map_total_n()` now call
`audit_seq()` and `audit_total_n()`.

* `grim_binomial()` and `grim_plot_rates()` reject sequence and total-n
output through `check_grim_map_basic()`: their rows are hypothetical
value sets, inconsistent by construction, so a p-value or rate over
them said nothing about the study, and was returned without a word.

* `check_audit_special()` is removed and `audit_cols_minimal()` loses
`name_test`; both only served the hint that `audit()` no longer needs.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Fix the review items of Oct 25
highlights.body:
* function_map() marked its error about a .fun whose arguments shadow
its internals as internal, which asked the user to report a bug. A user's
.fun with an argument named `data` triggers it, so it now goes through
abort_in_export() like the other checks at creation.

* map_value_sets() returns an empty vector for a wrapper with no formals
instead of failing on an empty cache key.

* .gitignore: `special-scripts/` made the three entries after it
redundant.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Rename vectorize_test() to map_value_sets()
highlights.body:
* It returns values, not a function, so it is no kind of Vectorize(); and
it serves grim_values(), grim_closest(), add_up_to(), and
is_percentage_of() too, which are no consistency tests.
* Drop the `frame` argument: it is always the caller's frame.
* Cache the missing() calls by the formals' names rather than the name the
wrapper was called under, which needed an identity check and an
empty-name branch. This makes fn_name_from_call() unused, so remove it.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: test: pin that an unavailable Camelot patch is recorded; use a placeholder id in the hygiene-guard probe
highlights.body:
The two Camelot patch installers (cell join, row-boundary tie) return False
when Camelot is absent or has changed shape; their scopes record an
unavailable event. Nothing asserted that, so the capability could vanish with
every table test green. Three tests now pin the event on both scopes and its
absence on a healthy install.

The hygiene guard's positive probe quoted a real-looking private ledger id.
It now uses a placeholder with the same shape.
highlights.author: Gilad Feldman

highlights.message: fix(diag): the non-statistic scan folds a soft hyphen to nothing, not to a dash
highlights.body:
S6 deletes U+00AD, so a URL with soft hyphens correctly becomes the clean URL.
The scan folded U+00AD to '-' and reported that strip as a rewritten URL on two
corpus papers, exiting 1 on a healthy tree. Adds a regression test with a
red control.
highlights.author: Gilad Feldman

highlights.message: fix(normalize): an Author Biographies heading ends the reference list
highlights.body:
The academic reference join ran past it and glued the heading onto the last
reference once the column order placed it there. 5 of 125 corpus papers
change, all at that heading. Canary audited in-session (6 papers; this was
the only finding absent from the previous release).

highlights.body: 27 ids in 19 files (all present before this release) are removed or replaced by what they referred to; test_public_repo_hygiene's internal-reference pattern now matches the id shape, with planted and clean controls. Watched red on 25 lines, green after.

highlights.message: test: pin G5c2 to pdftotext's order, assert the default column order, accept the reorder's method suffix; re-pin 9 extract_pdf checksums
highlights.body: With the general column reorder on by default, the four G5c2 papers no longer carry the stray footnote numbers above their headings, so G5c2 has nothing to rejoin there. Its guard tests now run on pdftotext's order, and a new test asserts each heading still resolves, without stacked numbers and idempotently, on the default order. The 9 checksum changes are reorder-only: all 40 tests in test_v2_backwards_compat and G5c2 pass on the old pins with DOCPLUCK_COLUMN_CORRECT_GENERAL=0.

highlights.message: test(perf): measure the interpreter itself, not a Windows venv launcher, in the CPU budget
highlights.body: Under a Windows virtual environment sys.executable is a launcher that starts the base interpreter as its child, so the measured process burned no CPU (0.016 s after 1.5 s of spinning) and no budget could fire. The base interpreter is now started directly with __PYVENV_LAUNCHER__, which runs it as the same venv in one process. test_cpu_budget: 3 failed -> 8 passed under the venv; 8 passed under the system interpreter before and after.

highlights.message: Read two-column pages by region, and turn the general column reorder on by default
highlights.body:
The left-then-right reorder of interleaved pages now runs behind a region
plan. The page body is cut at full-width blank bands; a table across the
gutter, or two two-column blocks stacked apart or in different type, leaves
the page in pdftotext's order, and a full-width table above or below the
columns is read in place. Bands with text on one side only join the column
flow. The column crops also give a rotated margin watermark its own crop when
a figure in the body has a rotated axis title.

Measured over the 125-paper corpus manifest against base: 190 pages in 55
papers change, every one a pure reorder (same words and characters), each
adjudicated by reading the page. DOCPLUCK_COLUMN_CORRECT_GENERAL=0 turns the
general path off. The banded path stays off.
